articleTitle: GLUING TECHNIQUES IN TRIANGULAR GEOMETRY
abstract: We discuss gluing of objects and gluing of morphisms in triangulated categories. We illustrate the results by producing, among other things, a Mayer‐Vietoris exact sequence involving Picard groups.

articleTitle: REAL BELYI THEORY
abstract: We develop a Belyi-type theory that applies to Klein surfaces, that is, (possibly non-orientable) surfaces with boundary which carry a dianalytic structure. In particular, we extend Belyi's famous theorem from Riemann surfaces to Klein surfaces.

articleTitle: CORRIGENDA
MOTIVIC INVARIANTS OF ARTIN STACKS AND ‘STACK FUNCTIONS’
abstract: An invariant Ƴ of quasiprojective K-varieties X with values in a commutative ring Λ is motivic if Ƴ(X) = Ƴ(Y) + Ƴ(X\ Y) for Y closed in X, and Ƴ(X × Y) = Ƴ(X)Ƴ(Y). Examples include Euler characteristics χ and virtual Poincaré and Hodge polynomials. We first define a unique extension Ƴ′ of Ƴ to finite type Artin K-stacks, which is motivic and satisfies Ƴ′([X/G]) = Ƴ(X)/Ƴ(G) when X is a K-variety, G a special K-group acting on X, and [X/G] is the quotient stack. This only works if Ƴ(G) is invertible in Λ for all special K-groups G, which excludes Ƴ = χ as χ(G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) = 0. But we can extend the construction to get round this.Then we develop the theory of stack functions on Artin stacks. These are a universal generalization of constructible functions on Artin stacks. There are several versions of the construction: the basic one, and variants ‘twisted’ by motivic invariants. We associate a ℚ-vector space or a Λ-module to each Artin stack, with functorial operations of multiplication, pullbacks ϕ* and pushforwards ϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf> under 1-morphisms, and so on. They will be important tools in the author's series on ‘Configurations in abelian categories’.

articleTitle: SPHERICAL SIMPLICES AND THEIR POLARS
abstract: This article is about spherical simplices in the unit sphere. One of the purposes is to give a relation of dihedral angles of a spherical simplex and its polar, and the other is to give two simple formulae of volumes of spherical simplices and their polars. We can calculate the volume of a spherical simplex and the sum of volumes of it and its polar from these formulae for the unit sphere in the odd- and even-dimensional Euclidean spaces, respectively.

articleTitle: NORMALIZERS OF NILPOTENT SUBGROUPS OF DIVISION RINGS
abstract: Let D be an arbitrary division ring and G a nilpotent subgroup of the multiplicative group D* of D of class at most 2 such that D is generated as a division ring by G and the centralizer in D of G. The normalizer of G in D* is computed precisely, which extends a theorem of M. Shirvani from finite-dimensional division algebras to arbitrary division rings.

articleTitle: SMALL C*-ALGEBRAS THAT FAIL TO HAVE SEPARABLE REPRESENTATIONS
abstract: It is shown that any σ-finite, wild AW*-algebra of type II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> fails to have non-trivial separable representations. Here a wild AW*-algebra means an AW*-algebra with no direct summand, which is *-isomorphic to a von Neumann algebra. Let be the σ-finite, wild type II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> AW*-algebra formed by taking the monotone complete tensor product of the Dixmier algebra D and a factor ℳ of type II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> acting on a separable Hilbert space. As both D and ℳ act on separable Hilbert spaces, it seems natural to describe as small and to ask the following question. Does have a non-trivial separable representation? The above described result answers negatively to this question. That is, fails to have non-trivial separable representations.

articleTitle: AUTOMORPHISMS OF PRO-p GROUPS OF FINITE VIRTUAL COHOMOLOGICAL DIMENSION
abstract: Let G be a pro-p group of finite cohomological dimension and type FP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> and T be a finite p-group of automorphisms of G. We prove that the group of fixed points of T in G is again a pro-p group of type FP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> (in particular it is finitely presented). Moreover, we prove that a pro-p group G of type FP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> and finite virtual cohomological dimension has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups.

articleTitle: ELEMENTS WITH THE SAME NORMAL CLOSURE IN A METABELIAN GROUP
abstract: It is known that in a free group, two elements a, b have the same normal closure if and only if the images of these elements have the same order in every finite quotient of the free group (Klyachko, 1999) or if and only if a is conjugate to b or b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> (Magnus, 1931). Here, we prove that the result of Klyachko remains true in a finitely generated soluble group of derived length d ≤ 2. An example shows that the property fails when d = 3. Also, we give a counterpart of Magnus's result in the context of metabelian nilpotent group.

articleTitle: OPTIMAL INTEGRABILITY CONDITION FOR THE LOG-SOBOLEV INEQUALITY
abstract: Let M denote a connected complete Riemannian manifold (possibly with a convex boundary), ρ the Riemannian distance function from a fixed point and V ∈ C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (M) such that dμ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</inf>≔ e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</sup> d x is a probability measure. For any K ≥ 0, we prove that K/2 is the infimum over all λ > 0 such that Ric<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> − Hess<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</inf> ≥ −K and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \rm v({\rm e^{\lambda\rho}}^2)$</tex> imply the log-Sobolev inequality for the Dirichlet form μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</inf>(|∇ f |<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: ALVIS–CURTIS DUALITY ON LOWERCASE q-SCHUR AND HECKE ALGEBRAS
abstract: We show that for a finite reductive group tensoring with a quotient of the complex inducing the Alvis–Curtis character duality induces a self-derived equivalence on a quotient of the group algebra. In the case of general linear groups, this equivalence realizes an equivalence between derived categories of q-Schur algebras. Furthermore, in the latter case, multiplication of the quotient complex by an idempotent induces an isomorphism with the two-sided q-analogue of the Coxeter complex.

articleTitle: THE DISTRIBUTION OF INTEGERS WITH AT LEAST TWO DIVISORS IN A SHORT INTERVAL
abstract: We estimate the density of integers which have more than one divisor in an interval (y, z] with z ≈ y + y/(log y)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">log 4 − 1</sup>. As a consequence, we determine the precise range of z such that most integers which have at least one divisor in (y, z] have exactly one such divisor.

articleTitle: AN ELEMENTARY PROOF OF THE ABRESCH–ROSENBERG THEOREM ON CONSTANT MEAN CURVATURE IMMERSED SURFACES IN 푊2 × ℝ AND ℍ2 × ℝ
abstract: We make explicit the centers and radii of the horizontal geodesic circles on a constant mean curvature surface with null Abresch–Rosenberg differential in 푊<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × ℝ and in ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × ℝ (horizontal horocycles are also determined) and prove that those centers project on to the same point, unless the complete surface is foliated by horocycles. This new visualization of the rotational and special surfaces classified by Abresch and Rosenberg is obtained in a direct way, just taking covariant derivatives of the unit normal along the flows of two global tangent fields. Moreover, this approach reveals that the special surfaces in ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × ℝ have constant intrinsic curvature K ≡ −1+4H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ∈ (−1, 0], so they form a non-rotational family of hyperbolic examples converging to a flat one, as 4H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ↗ 1.

articleTitle: REAL HYPERSURFACES IN A EUCLIDEAN COMPLEX SPACE FORM
abstract: Let M be an orientable connected and compact real hypersurface of the complex space form C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n + 1)/2</sup>. If the mean curvature α and the function f = g(Aξ, ξ) of hypersurface M satisfy the inequality n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>α<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ≤ (n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> − 1)δ + f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where ξ is the characteristic vector field, A is the shape operator and (n − 1)δ is the infimum of the Ricci curvatures of hypersurface M, then it is shown that α is a constant and M is the sphere S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>(α<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) in C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n + 1)/2</sup>.

articleTitle: JORDAN ISOMORPHISM OF PURELY INFINITE C*-ALGEBRAS
abstract: We prove that every unital bounded linear mapping from a unital purely infinite C*-algebra of real rank zero into a unital Banach algebra which preserves elements of square zero is a Jordan homomorphism. This entails a description of unital surjective spectral isometries as the Jordan isomorphisms in this setting.

articleTitle: ON A LIMITING RELATION BETWEEN RAMANUJAN'S ENTIRE FUNCTION Aq(z) AND θ-FUNCTIONS
abstract: We will use a discrete analogue of the classical Laplace method to show that the main term of the asymptotic expansions of certain entire functions, including Ramanujan's entire function A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>(z), can be expressed in terms of θ-functions.

articleTitle: SPECIAL SYMPLECTIC SIX-MANIFOLDS
abstract: We classify nilmanifolds with an invariant symplectic half-flat structure. We study the transverse or quotient geometry of six-manifolds with an SU (3)-structure preserved by a Killing vector field, giving characterizations in the symplectic half-flat and integrable case.

articleTitle: SMOOTH NORMS AND APPROXIMATION IN BANACH SPACES OF THE TYPE C(K)
abstract: Two results are proved about the Banach space X = C(K), where K is compact and Hausdorff. The first concerns smooth approximation: let m be a positive integer or ∞; we show that if there exists on X a non-zero function of class C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> with bounded support, then all continuous real-valued functions on X can be uniformly approximated by functions of class C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. The second result is that if X admits a norm, equivalent to the supremum norm, with locally uniformly convex dual norm, then X also admits an equivalent norm that is of class C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> (except at 0).

articleTitle: GENERATING SEQUENCES OF FUNCTIONS
abstract: We consider the problem of obtaining an arbitrary countable collection of functions with specific properties as a composition of finitely many functions with the same property. The functions investigated are continuous, Baire-n, Lebesgue or Borel measurable, increasing, and differentiable functions on [0, 1], and increasing functions on ℕ.

articleTitle: ON FREYD'S GENERATING HYPOTHESIS
abstract: Freyd's generating hypothesis in stable homotopy theory is revisited and new consequences and equivalent forms of it are derived. A surprising such consequence is that I, the Brown–Comenetz dual of the sphere and the source of many counterexamples in stable homotopy, is the cofibre of a self-map of a wedge of spheres. It is also shown that a consequence of the generating hypothesis, that the homotopy of a finite spectrum that is not a wedge of spheres can never be finitely generated as a module over π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>S, is in fact true for many finite torsion spectra.

articleTitle: CALIBRATED SUBMANIFOLDS OF ℝ7 AND ℝ8 WITH SYMMETRIES
abstract: The principal theory of this paper comprises a technique for constructing associative, coassociative and Cayley submanifolds of Euclidean space with symmetries, using first-order ordinary differential equations. Explicit examples of U(1)-invariant associative cones in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> and SU(2)-invariant Cayley 4-folds in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> are then produced using this method. Further examples of associative 3-folds are presented, which are ruled, and other systems of differential equations defining calibrated submanifolds in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> and ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> are given.

articleTitle: VECTOR FIELDS IN ℝ2 WITH MAXIMAL INDEX
abstract: We consider the method of Poincaré to investigate the local index of vector fields in the plane. If m is the degree of the first non-zero jet, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, of the vector field X at an isolated zero, we explore the geometry of the pencil generated by the coordinate functions of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> when the absolute value of the index of X, |ind (X)|, is m. We also find necessary and sufficient conditions for |ind (X)| to be m.

articleTitle: A BERNSTEIN-TYPE INEQUALITY FOR LOCALIZATIONS OF IWASAWA ALGEBRAS OF HEISENBERG PRO-p GROUPS
abstract: We prove a result about the possible dimensions of modules over the completed F group algebra of a Heisenberg pro-p group that are not torsion qua modules over the centre. We explain why this result is analogous to a result of Bernstein for modules over Weyl algebras in characteristic 0.

articleTitle: DISTRIBUTION OF ANGLES BETWEEN GEODESIC RAYS ASSOCIATED WITH HYPERBOLIC LATTICE POINTS
abstract: For every two points z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> in the upper-half plane ℍ, consider all elements γ in the principal congruence group Γ(N), acting on ℍ by fractional linear transformations, such that the hyperbolic distance between z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and γ z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is at most R > 0. We study the distribution of angles between the geodesic rays [z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, γ z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>] as R → ∞, proving that the limiting distribution exists independently of N and explicitly computing it. When z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, this is found to be the uniform distribution on the interval [−π/2, π/2].

articleTitle: DIFFERENCES OF ERGODIC AVERAGES FOR CESÀRO BOUNDED OPERATORS
abstract: We prove that the weighted differences of ergodic averages, induced by a Cesàro bounded, strongly continuous, one-parameter group of positive, invertible, linear operators on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>, 1 < p < ∞, converge almost every where and in the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-norm. We obtain first the boundedness of the ergodic maximal operator and the convergence of the averages.

articleTitle: INVARIANT FIELDS AND LOCALIZED INVARIANT RINGS OF p-GROUPS
abstract: It is well known that for a p-group, the invariant field is purely transcendental (T. Miyata, Invariants of certain groups I, Nagoya Math. J. 41 (1971), 69–73). In this note, we show that a minimal generating set of this field can be chosen as homogeneous invariants from the invariant ring. As a result, we show that the invariant ring localized at one suitable invariant is the localization of a polynomial subring at this same invariant. This second result is a generalization of a recent result of the first author for cyclic groups of order p (H. E. A. Campbell, Rings of invariants of representations of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> in characteristic p, preprint, 2006). As well, we specialize these results to this latter case.

articleTitle: BANACH ALGEBRAS WITH LARGE GROUPS OF UNITARY ELEMENTS
abstract: We study unitary Banach algebras, as defined by M. L. Hansen and R. V. Kadison in 1996, as well as some related concepts like maximal or uniquely maximal Banach algebras. We show that a norm-unital Banach algebra is uniquely maximal if and only if it is unitary and has minimality of the equivalent norm. We prove that every unitary semisimple commutative complex Banach algebra has a conjugate-linear involution mapping each unitary element to its inverse, and that, endowed with such an involution, becomes a hermitian *-algebra. The possibility of removing the requirement of commutativity in the above statement is also considered. The paper concludes by translating to real algebras some results previously known in the complex case. In particular, we show that every maximal semisimple finite-dimensional real Banach algebra is isometrically isomorphic to a real C*-algebra.

articleTitle: COARSE AND UNIFORM EMBEDDINGS INTO REFLEXIVE SPACES
abstract: Answering an old problem in nonlinear theory, we show that c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> cannot be coarsely or uniformly embedded into a reflexive Banach space, but that any stable metric space can be coarsely and uniformly embedded into a reflexive space. We also show that certain quasi-reflexive spaces (such as the James space) also cannot be coarsely embedded into a reflexive space and that the unit ball of these spaces cannot be uniformly embedded into a reflexive space. We give a necessary condition for a metric space to be coarsely or uniformly embeddable in a uniformly convex space.

articleTitle: CHARACTERISTIC NILPOTENT SUBGROUPS OF BOUNDED CO-RANK AND AUTOMORPHICALLY INVARIANT NILPOTENT IDEALS OF BOUNDED CODIMENSION IN LIE ALGEBRAS
abstract: It is proved that if a Lie algebra L has a nilpotent ideal of nilpotency class c and of finite codimension r, then L has also a nilpotent ideal of class ≤ c and of finite codimension bounded in terms of r and c that is invariant under all automorphisms of L. In a similar result for groups, the role of dimension is played by rank: if a group G has a normal nilpotent subgroup H of class c such that the quotient group G/H has finite rank r and H is either torsion-free or periodic, then G has also a characteristic nilpotent subgroup C of class ≤ c with quotient G/C of finite rank bounded in terms of r and c.

articleTitle: CONFORMAL MEASURES ASSOCIATED TO ENDS OF HYPERBOLIC n-MANIFOLDS
abstract: Let Γ be a non-elementary Kleinian group acting on the closed n-dimensional unit ball and assume that its Poincaré series converges at the exponent α. Let M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> be the Γ-quotient of the open unit ball. We consider certain families ℰ = {E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>} of open subsets of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M_\Gamma}\ ({\cup_{E\epsilon\varepsilon}}E)$</tex> is compact. The sets E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> are the ends of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> and ℰ is a complete collection of ends for M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>. We associate to each end E ∈ ℰ an α-conformal measure such that the measures corresponding to different ends are mutually singular if non-trivial. Additionally, each α-conformal measure for Γ on the limit set Λ(Γ) of Γ can be written as a sum of such conformal measures associated to ends E ∈ ℰ. In dimension 3, our results overlap with some results of Bishop and Jones (The law of the iterated logarithm for Kleinian groups, Cont. Math. 211 (1997), 17–50.).

articleTitle: ZERO-SUM PROBLEMS IN FINITE ABELIAN GROUPS AND AFFINE CAPS
abstract: For a finite abelian group G, let S(G) denote the smallest integer l such that every sequence S over G of length | S| ≥ l has a zero-sum subsequence of length exp (G). We derive new upper and lower bounds for S(G), and all our bounds are sharp for special types of groups. The results are not restricted to groups G of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${G=C_n^r}$</tex>, but they respect the structure of the group. In particular, we show <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm S(C_n^4)}$</tex> for all odd n, which is sharp if n is a power of 3. Moreover, we investigate the relationship between extremal sequences and maximal caps in finite geometry.

articleTitle: LARGE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN CONSECUTIVE PRIMES
abstract: We use a sieve method together with mean and large value results for Dirichlet polynomials to prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum p_{n+a} - p_n \ll x^{2/3}, \\p_{n+a} - p_n > x^{1/2} x \leq p_n \le2x$</tex> where p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is the nth prime number.

articleTitle: LANGLANDS DUALITY AND G2 SPECTRAL CURVES
abstract: We first demonstrate how duality for the fibres of the so-called Hitchin fibration works for the Langlands dual groups Sp(2m) and SO(2m + 1). We then show that duality for G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is implemented by an involution on the base space which takes one fibre to its dual. A formula for the natural cubic form is given and shown to be invariant under the involution.

articleTitle: FOUR-DIMENSIONAL CONFORMAL C-SPACES
abstract: We investigate the structure of conformal C-spaces, a class of Riemannian manifolds which naturally arises as a conformal generalization of the Einstein condition. A basic question is when such a structure is closed, or equivalently locally conformally Cotton. In dimension four, we obtain a full answer to this question and also investigate the incidence of the Bach condition on this class of metrics. This is related to earlier results obtained in the Einstein–Weyl context.
